blindSummary:
This state/province documents both legislative hostility and organised street violence against queer events more sharply than any other. In 2024-2025, pride events across the state were disrupted by coordinated far-right counter-mobilisations: a mob of more than 700 neo-fascists assembled at a mid-sized town's parade (summer 2024, the season's largest organised counter-protest, alongside nine further pride-event incidents statewide); in a second town (September 2025), a simultaneous counter-march through the town produced seven criminal offences and a formal investigation after a public fascist salute; in the state's largest city (2025), neo-fascists attempted to disrupt the parade with a counter-protest. The state also co-authored, with two peer states, an upper-chamber initiative to tighten the federal self-ID law - an organised multi-state attempt to roll back trans self-ID rights.

Mitigating factors: police protection let all events proceed without physical harm to attendees; the 2025 mid-sized-town parade ran under heavy police presence. The violence pattern is concentrated in small and mid-sized towns and rural areas rather than the major urban centres.
blindSourceSummaries: Research report on pride-event attacks as physical manifestations of the anti-queer backlash in this country: documents the pattern of counter-mobilisations against pride parades including this state/province's largest of the season; cites a 2023 official state survey in which 30% of inhabitants agreed homosexuality is 'unnatural' (up 7 points in two years), evidencing the social climate behind the street pattern.

Regional news outlet (20 Sep 2025): seven criminal offences were committed on the fringes of a pride weekend in this state/province as hundreds marched and a simultaneous counter-march crossed the town; police opened an investigation after a public fascist salute.

National news report (31 May 2025): pride participants marched through this state's largest city while neo-fascists staged a counter-protest attempting to disrupt the parade - the largest-city incident in the statewide pattern.

Regional public radio (2025): after a contested self-ID case involving a convicted far-right provocateur, this state, together with two peer states, demanded tightening of the federal self-determination law, alleging abuse of the self-ID right - a joint upper-chamber initiative to restrict how trans and intersex people use legal gender change; the legislative-hostility evidence for this state's co-authorship.

National daily (June 2025, paywalled lead): one mid-sized town's pride parade and its right-wing counter-demo - pride in the 'queer hinterland' facing aggressive right-wing extremists; describes the 2025 event under heavy police presence in a mid-sized town of this state/province, the setting of the 2024 mob of more than 700.
blindTangential: The same far-right mobilisation capacity that targets pride events also drives the state's broader culture-war posture (school gender-language bans elsewhere in the region), a general hostility climate that shapes how safe visible queerness feels even where no trans-specific law exists.
blindLocalsOnly: The self-determination law is federal; this state's upper-chamber push to tighten it, and registry-office practice under it, primarily affects residents changing legal gender rather than visitors.
